metadata.title: Five-modality progression and regression trees
metadata.purpose: Machine-readable handoff for training-app implementation and Claude review
metadata.important_note: The shared state machine is a product design. The modality-specific evidence supports the signals and templates, not the exact app thresholds or transition counts.

states.ADVANCE_ONE_LEVER: Progress one primary dose variable after target work, RPE, symptoms, technique, and recent comparable execution support it.
states.REPEAT: Repeat the same prescription when execution is borderline, data are uncertain, or confirmation is needed.
states.REDUCE_OR_STOP: Reduce or stop after pain, unsafe technique, marked performance failure, illness, or concerning symptoms.
states.HOLD_AFTER_ABSENCE: An absence is not a failed session; resume the last successful dose unless readiness or symptoms require reduction.
states.CARDIO_PASS_MECHANICAL_FAIL: The cardiovascular signal reached its target but the prescribed mechanical/technical work was not completed; do not advance.
states.REASSESS: Recheck device, setup, sensor, recovery, recent load, and benchmark protocol before changing the prescription.

pre_session_screen.question: Pain, acute illness, unsafe setup, or unsafe technique today?

actions: stop or reduce the provoking task
route persistent or concerning symptoms for appropriate assessment

session_type.question: Was the session missed, steady, threshold-oriented, VO2-oriented, or sprint/interval?

actions: check readiness if the absence was illness-, pain-, or fatigue-related

steady_completion.question: Was duration completed with acceptable RPE, sustainable technique, and no concerning symptoms?

quality_completion.question: Was controlled hard work completed with stable quality and no meaningful RPE/output mismatch?

interval_completion.question: Were prescribed repetitions and work completed with acceptable output trend, recovery, RPE, and technique?

sprint_completion.question: Was the sprint safely completed with the intended technique and without concerning symptoms?

confirm_recent_stability.question: Are recent comparable exposures stable enough to justify a product-level progression?

actions: change only one primary dose variable
store the prior and new dose
re-evaluate total internal and external load
do not add a second progression variable
repeat if the issue was small and non-painful
reduce one dose variable if the issue recurs or output/technique deteriorates
record cardiovascular and mechanical outcomes separately
repeat or reduce after reviewing the local limiter

global_constraints: Do not use one heart-rate value as the sole completion criterion for short intervals.
Do not treat two consecutive misses as a validated demotion law.
Do not treat two or three successful exposures as a published physiological requirement; it is a configurable product confirmation heuristic.
Do not use HRR >12 bpm as a healthy-athlete progression gate.
Distinguish absence, sensor failure, pain, illness, deliberate rest, and failed execution.

phases.known_template: NHS Couch to 5K uses 3 runs/week over 9 weeks, begins with 1-minute running bouts alternated with 1:30 walking, and finishes with 30 minutes continuous running.
advance_levers: less walking within the published plan
regress_if: cannot complete the planned walk/run without loss of control
phases.benchmark: Use completed walk/run or submax duration; maximal testing is optional and should not be first-session onboarding.
Submax duration, 1-mile/5K, or Cooper-style field test only after familiarity; preserve protocol metadata.
Use threshold/cruise completion and RPE; do not require HR-zone time in short repetitions.

advance_levers: recovery reduction one variable at a time
phases.benchmark: Completed repetitions and pace; HR is secondary because short interval structure changes time above VO2max.

impact_screen.question: Pain, illness, gait change, or impact-sensitive symptoms?

walk_run_completion.question: Can the planned walk/run be completed with controlled form?

easy_stability.question: Is easy duration stable across comparable exposures?

add_duration_or_reduce_walk.action: Advance one lever from the published plan or configured product dose.

shorten_or_repeat.action: Repeat or shorten running bouts; do not progress intensity.

repeat.action: Repeat the last successful dose and reassess symptoms/RPE.

stop_or_refer.action: Stop the provoking work and route persistent/concerning symptoms appropriately.

primary_load: pace/500 m when device and protocol match

phases.known_template: British Rowing beginner plan begins with 1-minute low/1-minute rest ×5; Concept2 describes approximately 18–22 spm as technique/rhythm context.
phases.benchmark: Use submax duration or repeatable distance before optional 2k.

phases.known_template: Concept2 describes approximately 24–28 spm as steady-rowing context; rate alone is not intensity.
phases.benchmark: Store monitor, drag/damper context, distance, time, stroke rate, RPE, and technique notes.

advance_levers: higher rate only after stable sequence
phases.benchmark: Optional 2k/5k/30-minute test for trained/familiar users; not a required beginner test.

row_screen.question: Back, rib, shoulder, wrist, hip pain or unsafe catch/finish?

low_rate_control.question: Can sequence and posture be repeated at low rate?

technique_only.action: Shorten pieces and practise technique around the beginner/low-rate context.

steady_completion.question: Was low/medium work completed with stable stroke quality?

progress_one_lever.action: Increase duration, one piece, distance, or later rate; never all at once.

repeat_or_reduce.action: Repeat or reduce piece length/rate while preserving technique and recovery.

stop_or_reduce.action: Stop or reduce; persistent symptoms require appropriate assessment.

phases.known_template: Concept2 beginner programme uses 2–3 sessions/week over 6 weeks and includes 1-minute hard/1-minute easy, 30/30, 250 m, 1000 m, 1500 m, and 2000 m work.
phases.benchmark: Use repeatable 1000 m or submax duration for beginners; optional 2000 m after familiarity.

regress_if: local upper-body fatigue changes the hinge/pull
phases.benchmark: No accepted universal SkiErg FTP equivalent; use personal same-device results.
Use completed pieces and technique; do not use HR-zone time alone for short work.

upper_body_screen.question: Shoulder, elbow, rib, lumbar, hip pain or unsafe hinge/finish?

technique_control.question: Can the athlete repeat the hinge and finish without arm-dominant pulling?

technique_only.action: Use short easy pieces and technical practice; do not add interval density.

steady_completion.question: Was comfortable distance/duration completed with stable technique?

progress_one_lever.action: Increase duration/distance before hard density; later increase one interval lever.

repeat_or_reduce.action: Repeat or reduce distance/work duration/repetitions while preserving recovery.

stop_or_reduce.action: Stop the provoking dose and route persistent symptoms appropriately.

primary_load: cycling-specific watts/FTP when protocol is known

phases.known_template: British Cycling novice plan uses 3 rides/week and progresses weekly riding time; it is a coaching template, not a universal injury law.
regress_if: pain, unsafe fit, illness, inability to pedal smoothly, unusual RPE
phases.benchmark: Use duration/distance first; store bike, power meter, and protocol.

phases.known_template: Coggan endurance zone is 56–75% FTP when a valid cycling-specific FTP is available.
phases.benchmark: Do not display FTP zones when FTP protocol is unknown or when the device is an air bike.

phases.known_template: Coggan threshold 91–105% FTP and VO2 106–120% FTP are practical cycling controls; FTP95 and ramp estimates are conventions with individual error.
phases.benchmark: Store FTP test type: ramp, 20-minute, 60-minute, lab, or other. Never silently merge values.

cycle_screen.question: Pain, illness, unsafe fit, or inability to pedal smoothly?

ftp_context.question: Is a cycling-specific benchmark and protocol known?

power_control.question: Can the planned power/duration be completed with acceptable RPE and technique?

rpe_duration_control.action: Use duration, RPE, cadence, and HR trend; do not pretend FTP is known.

progress_one_lever.action: Increase duration, repetitions, power, or reduce recovery one at a time.

repeat_or_reduce.action: Repeat or reduce power/work/repetitions; check fit, fatigue, and protocol.

stop_or_refit.action: Stop, correct fit, recover, or route symptoms appropriately.

phases.known_template: No peer-reviewed universal starting duration/frequency was located. Manufacturer setup/safety and study familiarisation are the evidence base; any 5–10 minute or 1–2 sessions/week default is a product heuristic, not a sourced rule.
phases.benchmark: No maximal test on first exposure. Use submax duration and RPE/technique.

phases.known_template: Use duration, conversational/RPE control, and sustainable rhythm. Manufacturer 65–80% calculated HRmax and study 75% HRR are examples, not universal air-bike zones.
phases.benchmark: Same-device submax duration or optional field test after familiarisation; no universal calorie/min or distance standard.

phases.known_template: No universal air-bike VT/LT, RPM, watt, calorie, or FTP boundary. Use personal lab/device threshold or controlled hard RPE/work prescription.
phases.benchmark: Threshold test only with device-specific or laboratory anchor; otherwise call it controlled hard work, not a validated threshold zone.

phases.known_template: 10/5 and 20/10 have a four-week recreationally-active intervention; Echo 15/45 and 40/20 variants have a small eight-week active-adult study; supervised all-extremity 4×4 protocols exist in older/clinical populations.
regress_if: cardio target reached but work incomplete
phases.benchmark: Training protocols are not reliability standards. Do not label 30/30 or 60/60 validated for beginners.

phases.known_template: Device-specific staged ramp/VO2peak testing is the strongest reliability category. Sprint, 5-minute, 10-minute, 2-mile, and Wingate-style tests lack universal combined-air-bike reliability/validity.
advance_levers: only after familiarisation: repetitions, work duration, output, or recovery density
phases.benchmark: Store device/protocol; compare only within the same device/protocol. Maximal test is optional, not onboarding.

airbike_safety_screen.question: Pain, illness, unsafe setup, or unsafe mounting/dismounting?

coordination.question: Can the athlete coordinate linked handles and pedals at easy effort with stable trunk/shoulder technique?

familiarisation.action: Use submaximal easy exposure, repeatable rhythm, and no maximal benchmark. Record local limiter and technique.

steady_readiness.question: Can easy duration be completed with acceptable RPE, rhythm, technique, and local fatigue?

repeat_or_reduce_steady.action: Repeat or shorten duration/output; do not add interval density.

choose_quality_phase.question: Is there a personal/device-specific threshold or is this only a controlled-hard prescription?

threshold_work.question: Were work blocks completed with stable output, RPE, recovery, and technique?

controlled_hard_work.action: Use RPE, completed work, and same-device output; do not display universal air-bike threshold zones.

confirm_and_progress.action: After comparable stability, advance one lever: duration, reps, work length, output, or recovery density.

repeat_or_reduce_intervals.action: Repeat or reduce one variable; inspect local fatigue, technique, setup, sleep, and device data.

cardio_pass_mechanical_fail.action: Record cardiovascular target as reached but mechanical session as incomplete; do not progress.

stop_or_safety_route.action: Stop the provoking dose; record body region/reason and route persistent or concerning symptoms appropriately.

local_failure.if: cardiovascular signal reached but shoulder, arm, trunk, or leg fatigue prevents planned work

directly_supported: device-specific staged ramp/VO2peak with gas analysis
